risk_if_not_implemented:
Without Service Delivery
(Business Process Support), security, compliance and resilience activities may lack direction, ownership and executive support, leaving required controls unperformed. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Business / Service Interruption (R-BC-1), Failure to Support Business / Mission Objectives (R-GV-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9), Workforce Shortage / Loss of Critical Skills / Labor Disruption (MT-25).

compensating_control_1.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
compensating_control_1.description:
Mechanisms exist to operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
(1) Routine operations; and
(2) Adverse conditions.
compensating_control_1.justification:
Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) (BCD-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Service Delivery
(Business Process Support) (OPS-05) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Capacity & Performance Management
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the implementation of capacity management controls to ensure optimal system performance to meet expected and anticipated future capacity requirements.
compensating_control_2.justification:
Capacity & Performance Management (CAP-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Service Delivery
(Business Process Support) (OPS-05) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
